title: Landon Hotel Application
summary: Backend REST controllers for an Angular hotel app, containerized with Docker and deployed to Microsoft Azure.
description: A full-stack hotel application. I developed the backend REST controllers that power the Angular frontend, then packaged the app as a Docker image and deployed it to a Microsoft Azure resource. Source control and workflow were managed in GitLab.
highlights: Built backend REST controllers for an Angular frontend
Created a Docker image and deployed it to Microsoft Azure
Kept an organized workflow with GitLab source control

title: Travel Agency Application
summary: A Spring Boot backend with REST APIs and a JPA/Hibernate database layer for a travel agency Angular frontend.
description: A Spring Boot backend for a travel agency application with an Angular frontend. I implemented the REST APIs and integrated a database using JPA/Hibernate, using class diagrams and ERDs to design entities that worked with the frontend.
highlights: Implemented REST APIs and integrated a database with JPA/Hibernate
Designed entities from class diagrams and ERDs
Managed source control and workflow in GitLab

title: Storage Auction App
summary: Gathers local storage unit auctions and dynamically predicts their value based on photos.
description: An app that gathers local storage unit auctions in one place and dynamically predicts value based on photos. The project is split into a backend and a frontend and runs together with Docker Compose.
highlights: Collects local storage unit auctions in one place
Predicts value dynamically from listing photos
Separate backend and frontend, run together with Docker Compose

title: Hotel Reservation App
summary: A database-driven hotel booking app built by a four-person Scrum team: room search, booking, checkout, and an admin dashboard.
description: A database-driven hotel reservation web app built over a semester with a team of four, most of us new to Java Servlets. I implemented server-side functionality with Java Servlets and integrated features with a MySQL database. Users can browse rooms by specific criteria, book, check out, and edit or review bookings; admins can manage rooms and reservations.
highlights: Server-side features built with Java Servlets on a MySQL database
Worked in Scrum sprints to plan, build, troubleshoot, and integrate changes
Tested with JUnit; shipped through tagged GitHub releases

title: Unity Drag-and-Drop Inventory
summary: A reusable drag-and-drop inventory and toolbar framework for Unity 3D games.
description: A reusable inventory framework in C# and Unity 3D that I can drop into any game project. Item, inventory, toolbar, slot, and database components keep item management and UI interaction organized, and inheritance supports specialized item types on top of a central item database.
highlights: Drag-and-drop inventory with a toolbar to move items between slots
Item inheritance for specialized item types
Centralized item database using the singleton pattern

title: Stock Viewing Application
summary: A React app that pulls stock data from an external REST API and lets you search and view market information.
description: A React web application that consumes an external REST API to retrieve and display stock information. It uses reusable components and asynchronous API requests to present data dynamically, with an interactive interface for searching and viewing market information.
highlights: Reusable React components
Asynchronous requests to an external REST API
Interactive search and market views

title: CLI Shell Simulator
summary: A basic Linux shell with pipes, input/output redirection, and core commands like cat, cd, pwd, mkdir, and ls.
description: A C++ program that mimics a basic Linux shell, supporting pipes and input/output redirection along with commands like cat, cd, pwd, mkdir, and ls. Built in four major pieces over a semester, it taught me a lot about Linux and C++ system calls. See the GitHub repo for the full command list.
highlights: Pipes and input/output redirection
Built-in commands: cat, cd, pwd, mkdir, ls, and more
Hands-on with Linux process and file system calls

title: LRU Cache Simulator
summary: A cache simulator that tracks access order and evicts the least recently used block.
description: A C++ program that simulates cache memory with a Least Recently Used replacement policy, applying data structures and algorithms to track cached elements and pick replacement candidates efficiently. It taught me a lot about how cache memory works and how to handle memory addresses.
highlights: Least Recently Used (LRU) replacement policy
Efficient tracking of cached elements with data structures
Working directly with memory addresses and cache blocks
